messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The proposed algorithm is able to deal with certain amount of noise when generating realistic images." -- cites: E1 (Section L): quote "The results show that the proposed algorithm is able to deal with certain amount of noise when generating realistic images."
2. "The proposed algorithm can handle a wide scope of input patch variations, including different skin colors, textures, hairstyles, expressions, and orientations." -- cites: E1 (Section L): quote "The results show that the proposed algorithm can handle a wide scope of input patch variations. For example, inputs contain different skin colors in the first column."
3. "The presence of noise in the input image does not necessarily degrade the quality of the generated images; instead, it can lead to the generation of realistic images with reasonable skin color and overall shape." -- cites: E1 (Section L): quote "The results show that the proposed algorithm is able to deal with certain amount of noise when generating realistic images."; E2 (Section Figure 9): quote "Figure 9: Examples of generated results when the input image contains noises. We add a Gaussian noise at each pixel of Input 3. Gen 1 and Gen M1 are generated without noises. Gen 2 and Gen M2 are generated with noises."
4. "The presence of noise in the input image can lead to realistic images being generated with reasonable skin color and overall shape, even when the input contains different skin colors." -- cites: E1 (Section L): quote "For example, inputs contain different skin colors in the first column. In this case, it is not desirable to exactly preserve inputs since it will generate a face image with two different skin colors. The proposed algorithm generates an image with a reasonable skin color as well as the overall shape."

Cited evidence:
[E1] (text, Section L, page 8): Figure 9 shows the results when input patches are degraded by noises. We apply the mean zero Gaussian noise at each pixel of the third input patch with the standard deviation of 0.1 (column 1-4) and 0.5 (column 5-8). The results show that the proposed algorithm is able to deal with certain amount of noise when generating realistic images. Figure 10 shows generated images and masks when input patches are obtained from different persons. The results show that the proposed algorithm can handle a wide scope of input patch variations. For example, inputs contain different skin colors in the ﬁrst column. In this case, it is not desirable to exactly preserve inputs since it will generate a face image with two different skin colors. The proposed algorithm generates an image with a reasonable skin color as well as the overall shape. Other cases include with or without sunglasses (column 2), different skin textures (column 3), hairstyle variations (column 4 and 5), and various expressions and orientations. Despite large variations, the proposed algorithm is able to generate realistic images.
[E2] (text, Section Figure 9, page 8): Figure 9: Examples of generated results when the input im- age contains noises. We add a Gaussian noise at each pixel of Input 3. Gen 1 and Gen M1 are generated without noises. Gen 2 and Gen M2 are generated with noises.
